cells.tense: This steadiness of yours is here right now, with the pen.
cells.ask: Next time someone hands you a feeling, sit with it whole and do not fix it, just once. Notice what the room does without your help.
cells.core: There is a way you stay in a room while it is feeling something, and the room does not go sideways. You are not managing anyone and you are not going under with them. People find the middle of themselves near you and you do not have to work for it — you hold the feeling without absorbing it or handing it back.\n\nWhat this balance is free to feed next is something that stands on its own, so every steady room does not run through your hands. That is the next thing to build, and it is not a loss. It is the difference between holding a space and being the only floor under it.
cells.sheetLine: Feelings settle near you and you are not bracing.
cells.verb: holding the space of feeling without taking it over
cells.place: standing where nothing has chosen its shape yet

cells.tense: You keep arriving ahead of a steadiness that has not been asked for yet.
cells.ask: Let one feeling stay in the room without handling it. Watch it for a full minute and let it be unresolved.
cells.core: You can take a hard feeling arriving and stay open to it instead of bracing or shutting it out. That is the working version — attuned, in the room, not drowning.\n\nThe trouble now is timing. You are steadying rooms no one has walked into, reaching for weight that has not been set down, softening things before they know they need softening. The attunement is real; it has just run ahead of what is here. What this balance is free to feed next is staying with what is actually in the room rather than what might arrive. Tending what is here is one thing. Carrying what nobody handed you is another, and you can set that one down without losing anything you value.

cells.tense: The tending stopped somewhere and you still stand at that closed door.
cells.ask: Name one true thing about what you feel to one person. The saying is the whole point, not the feeling.
cells.core: You know the version where the feeling lands in you and stays — in the room with it, not swept off by it. That is still inside what you do.\n\nWhere you are now, it arrives less. The room still finds its feet near you, but you stay at the wall and watch instead of arriving with it. Not cold — nearer to unplugged, standing at the edge and seeing how the room goes before you step in. There is nothing to push and nothing to force open. Say one true thing about yourself and say it plainly to one person, because naming is the way the present comes back through. What you feel will follow the saying, not the other way round, and the saying does not have to be brave — just accurate.

cells.tense: You are already holding the room and calling it the room holding itself.
cells.ask: Say out loud that the calm in one room is yours doing. One sentence, then let it stand unqualified.
cells.core: Holding a room while it feels something is already what you do, and it works — people ease near you and nothing is forced.\n\nWhat you strip out is the credit. You say the mood lifted, the meeting got easier, and not once that your own way of being there is what did it. Standing in a place where nothing has taken shape, you still pick what grows, and then you give the credit to the thing that grew. It is your attention doing the work, and that sentence is the cheapest claim to take back. Say one about a room you settled, as a sentence about you, with no softening tacked on the end.
